long_biography.plain_text:
Fragmented European payment processing gave Rudolf Booker the opportunity behind Payvision. Banks still handled gateways, fraud and risk functions separately, while American providers had begun packaging them into fuller services. Booker and co-founder Gijs op de Weegh adapted that model for European merchants and banks.

An early New York office helped the team study independent sales organisations and build Visa and Mastercard acquiring propositions. Payvision combined gateways with reporting, liability assessment and risk management, eventually running cross-border transactions through one platform. That integrated approach allowed the privately built company to expand across Europe, Asia and the United States.
